newsitem.title: USA: Hilton extends ITT offer, appeals ruling.
newsitem.headline: Hilton extends ITT offer, appeals ruling.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Thursday extended its $55 per share tender offer for ITT Corp and said it has appealed a U.S. District Court ruling that allows ITT to delay its annual meeting until mid-November.
That ruling, issued by Judge Philip Pro in Las Vegas on Monday, effectively put Hilton's $6.5 billion cash and stock offer on hold until shareholders can vote on the proposal at an annual meeting.
In the meantime, Hilton extended the tender offer until midnight EDT on May 30. It said so far only 1.5 million of about 122.7 million outstanding ITT shares have been tendered.
Hilton first made the offer on January 27. Since that time it has extended the bid twice. At the time of its most recent extension, on March 28, Hilton said 1.5 million shares had been tendered.
Early in February, ITT rejected Hilton's bid as inadequate and set about refocusing its business strategy on core assets in hotels and gaming and shedding non-core assets.

It has since sold its stake in French Telecommunications company Alcatel Altsholm for $830 million and signed an agreement to sell its partnership position in Madison Square Garden Inc, owner of the famous sports arena and two sports teams, for $650 million.

Hilton sued ITT in federal court asking Judge Pro to force ITT to hold its annual meeting in mid-May, when it has traditionally held the shareholder gathering. Hilton has nominated a slate of directors to unseat ITT's current board, and if elected Hilton's directors would approve the offer.
ITT argued that its bylaws and Nevada state law allowed it to delay calling a meeting until mid-November, and Judge Pro agreed. ITT still has not set a date for the meeting.
Hilton has said it will pursue its bid for ITT all the way to a shareholder vote.
